method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 64 covers N/N 1/2/O/O 1/2 and sheet 65 covers O 1/2/P/P 1/2/Q, so Ave O 1/2 is the only shared corridor; both plates print 'AVENUE O 1/2' in this gutter and each prints the other's number beside it ('65' on sheet 64, '64' on sheet 65). The cross-street run changes hundred-block exactly here: on sheet 64 the block against the avenue reads 1701/1703/1705/1707/1709/1711 and 1713/1715/1717/1719/1721/1723 with evens 1702-1712 and 1714/1716/1718/1720/1722/1724; sheet 65 starts the next hundred at 1801/1803/1805/1807/1809. One avenue west on sheet 64 the change is 16xx->17xx at Avenue O (1623/1624 printed beyond it). The avenue frontage runs interlock across the gutter at the same y: over native y 1500-2100 sheet 64's east block face carries the evens 3102,3104,3106...3120 and sheet 65's west block face the odds 3101,3103,3105...3117 - the two sides of the 31st-32nd segment of Ave O 1/2.
note: Detection candidates (64: 2775/1755/736; 65: 754/1765/2777) are mid-block lines. '70'' is printed mid-avenue on sheet 65 at native x 180 (at y~360, where the east block face is 285) - i.e. exactly on the drafted centre, confirming the 210 px (70') width. Both faces were read over native y 1500-2100 to match bands: sheet 64 west face 3057.5 (+105), sheet 65 east face 264 (-105). Both plates are tilted ~0.8 deg, so these corridor x's are the values at mid-sheet y.
